releases.headline: Follow several services in one terminal view
releases.summary: Combine live local log files, retain their source labels and keep more consecutive history on screen.

changes.change: Start a continuously followed, source-tagged stream with -m. Existing events and each live polling batch are sorted by parsed timestamps.
changes.benefit: Inspect API, worker and authentication events together while retaining the filename beside each event.

changes.change: Use -l to display three consecutive pages: p-2, p-1 and Current. Tab or 4 cycles line, table and long-split views.
changes.benefit: Keep more adjacent history visible in a wide terminal. Works with a single file or the live merged stream.

changes.change: Changes made with T and Tab / 4 are saved in the Flik configuration.
changes.benefit: Resume with your preferred theme and layout on the next launch.

releases.commands:
flik -m api.log worker.log auth.log
flik -m -l api.log worker.log auth.log
releases.limits: Live merge sorts each polling batch, not all future arrivals: late events stay appended. Initial contents are loaded into memory and the temporary merged file grows. Truncation is detected when size decreases; replacement with a same-size or larger file can miss events. The three columns are consecutive pages, not one column per service.

releases.headline: Inspect more formats and investigate structured events
releases.summary: Broader structured-log support and investigation tools reduce the manual preparation needed before inspecting cloud, web and system logs.

changes.change: Adds CloudWatch and Google Cloud Logging field handling, Logfmt detection, auth/syslog enrichment, extended access logs and named custom regex formats.
changes.benefit: Inspect fields from more existing log formats without first converting each file to a common schema.

changes.change: Adds correlation identifier extraction, the J JSON inspector and nested JSON completion in search and filter editors.
changes.benefit: Locate identifiers and inspect nested payloads while refining an investigation.

changes.change: The S dashboard can switch from its default sample to a full indexed-file scan with a. Live error-rate alerting is also available.
changes.benefit: Choose between a quick sampled overview and a broader count; keep the scope of the result explicit.

changes.change: Adds global TOML configuration, modular format definitions, native Windows binaries and the Homebrew tap.
changes.benefit: Reuse settings and install a prebuilt binary on the supported platform.

releases.limits: Field extraction depends on the input format. The default S dashboard remains sampled until a full scan is selected. Correlation identifiers help investigation but do not establish causality.

releases.headline: A local interactive workspace for log investigation
releases.summary: The initial release established interactive filtering, context and navigation for local files and piped streams.

changes.change: Background byte-offset indexing supports direct navigation through local log files.
changes.benefit: Move through a file and refine the visible result while indexing progresses.

changes.change: Stack include/exclude conditions and use smart find to retain surrounding lines.
changes.benefit: Inspect the evidence around an error instead of retaining only matching lines.

changes.change: Includes independent split panes, time and frequency tools, request correlation workflows, incident export and session save/restore.
changes.benefit: Keep the investigation state and source context together while moving between questions.

releases.limits: The byte-offset index still uses memory proportional to line count. Initial distribution covered Linux and macOS. This version does not include the continuously followed CLI multi-file merge or the three-column layout added in 0.3.0.
